recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Future editors may separately tidy the grammar in the HTTP note introduced by the later interaction terminology cleanup, but FHIR-7687 itself is correctly reconciled without source changes.
issue_request: FHIR-7687 asked for delete/history-specific caveats using Provenance and Consent to prevent unauthorized delete/history access. The Published resolution was Not Persuasive with Modification: do not embed a specific policy in the REST specification, but extend security guidance to note that operations are subject to RBAC, ABAC, consent, and related authorization controls.
initial_application: Jira's application comment cites svn revision 6464. Git-svn commit ae3042ca1e07b476a53c38836836edbf5255a3a2 corresponds to that revision and added the HTTP page note that most operations require authentication, operations that do are subject to RBAC and/or ABAC, and some operations may depend on appropriate consent.
additional_context: The current build-scope source still lists http.html and security.html in publish.ini. source/http.html links to the Security page and retains the RBAC/ABAC/consent note, while source/security.html has broader Authorization/Access Control guidance covering RBAC, ABAC, consent policy inputs, REST access methods, AuditEvent recording, and Provenance/Consent linkage. A later FHIR-40957 cleanup changed some 'operation' wording to 'interaction' in the same note, causing awkward singular/plural wording but not changing the FHIR-7687 authorization substance.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current specification already reflects the accepted general security guidance, and adding a delete/history-specific policy rule would conflict with the final resolution's rejection of embedding policy in the REST specification.

related_jiras.note: A later terminology cleanup changed 'operations' to 'interaction' in the same HTTP authorization note; it explains the current wording difference but does not require deciding FHIR-40957 here.
